name: Marker Cone
summary: Freehand dense-scene selection: the hand points a cone and moves a depth marker along it, and the object closest to the marker is selected; raising the other hand confirms.
howItWorks: Hand movement in a vertical plane steers the cone; moving the hand towards or away from the screen moves the marker along the cone's axis, combining cone-casting with the depth-marker idea of Depth Ray and the closest-object rule of the 3D Bubble Cursor. Because any motion of the pointing hand changes the selection, a 'hands up' gesture with the other hand confirms. Using a Kinect and a stereoscopic large display, menu cone (2.17 s) was significantly faster than marker cone (3.85 s) with no difference in errors, had lower physical demand and effort, and was preferred.
limitations: High physical demand; the marker is hard to control.

relationships.note: Applies the depth marker to a cone.

review.notes: Coded from the Computers & Graphics full text (Study 1). Environment coded projection (stereoscopic large display).
